name: The Historical Books (Former Prophets): Covenant History

objectives.text: Name Joshua, Judges, Samuel, and Kings as the books that tell the story of Israel living in the land God promised
Retell the story of the walls of Jericho falling when Israel obeyed the Lord's instructions
Retell the story of the Lord calling the boy Samuel in the night
Retell the story of David and Goliath and identify David's words that the battle belongs to the Lord
Identify Deborah and Gideon as judges the Lord raised up to rescue Israel
Explain why Israel's request for a king to be like the nations displeased the Lord and Samuel
Describe how Joshua led Israel into Canaan and how the text shows the Lord keeping every promise about the land
Summarize the repeated cycle of sin, oppression, crying out, and deliverance in the book of Judges
Retell the contest between Elijah and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel and explain what it showed about the Lord
Explain the Lord's covenant promise to David of a house, a kingdom, and a throne established forever
Explain how Solomon's idolatry and Rehoboam's harsh answer led to the division of the kingdom into Israel and Judah
Sequence the major periods of the Former Prophets from conquest through the judges, the united monarchy, the divided monarchy, and the falls of Samaria and Jerusalem
Compare faithful kings such as Hezekiah and Josiah with unfaithful kings such as Ahab using the standard of covenant loyalty the books apply
Explain the reasons the narrator gives for the exile of the northern kingdom to Assyria and of Judah to Babylon
Explain why the Hebrew canon calls Joshua through Kings the Former Prophets and distinguish this grouping from the Historical Books of the English Bible
Analyze how the Former Prophets judge Israel's history by the covenant blessings and curses set out in Deuteronomy
Analyze the role of prophets such as Nathan and Elijah in confronting kings with the word of the Lord
Explain how the gift of the land and its later loss are tied to Israel's covenant relationship with the Lord
Apply attention to narrative features such as the regnal formula and the narrator's verdict that a king did right or evil in the sight of the Lord when interpreting a passage in Kings
Analyze Joshua's covenant renewal at Shechem and the people's pledge to serve the Lord alone
Trace the decline from conquest to exile by identifying patterns of idolatry and covenant breaking that recur across the Former Prophets
Construct a synchronized timeline of the kings of Israel and Judah and their prophets using the regnal formulas in Kings
Compare the account of Sennacherib's invasion in Kings with Assyrian records of the same campaign
Analyze how the New Testament presents Jesus as the promised Son of David who fulfills the Davidic covenant as the tradition confesses Christ's kingly office
Evaluate the character of David as a man after God's own heart in light of his sin with Bathsheba and his response to Nathan
Defend the justice of God in sending Israel and Judah into exile using the narrator's explanation and the repeated prophetic warnings
Evaluate interpretations of the conquest of Canaan in light of the texts on Canaanite sin, God's judgment, and the inclusion of Rahab
Compose a synthesis of the theme of God's faithfulness despite human failure across the Former Prophets including the hope signaled by Jehoiachin's release

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (book names, David and Goliath, request for a king, Judges cycle, kingdom split, good and bad kings, Deuteronomic perspective, prophets confronting kings, land and covenant, decline to exile, synchronized timeline, David's character, justice of God in exile, faithfulness synthesis). Dropped the vague blessing and trouble observation as folded into the Deuteronomic objective and reworked the thin Exile item into an explanation of the narrator's reasons. Added Jericho, Samuel's call, Deborah and Gideon, Joshua's entry, Elijah on Carmel, the Davidic covenant and its fulfillment in Christ, period sequencing, the Former Prophets canonical label, narrative regnal formulas, the Shechem covenant renewal, Assyrian records, conquest ethics, and Jehoiachin's release. Replaced Lamentations with texts from Kings, added verse anchors throughout, and cited WSC Q23 and Q26, WCF 2.1, and WCF 5.1 only where they state the doctrine.
